newsitem.title: UK: Poland slams Western critics of NATO expansion.
newsitem.headline: Poland slams Western critics of NATO expansion.

text.p: Polish Foreign Minister Dariusz Rosati on Wednesday attacked Western critics of NATO expansion, saying they could spark a conflict in Europe by expressing doubts about the wisdom of enlarging the 16-nation alliance.

"There is some opposition in Western countries by those who ask why Russia should be antagonised...this is a very dangerous way of thinking about security," Rosati told the Royal United Services Institute think-tank.

NATO is due to hold a summit in Madrid in July when it will invite at least three former Soviet allies -- widely believed to be Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic -- to start talks on becoming members.
Some Western politicians and experts say expanding NATO would stir up dangerous passions among Russian hardliners at a time of widespread dissatisfaction over low living standards.

"If you think that central Europe can be left as a grey zone partly because Russia doesn't pose a threat now, it's a remote area, it would involve some cost -- this is a very dangerous concept," said Rosati.
NATO is trying to work out a charter regulating its links with Russia to take into account the planned expansion, which Moscow says threatens its security.

"If central Europe is left to itself it will always be an area which will be contested. All doubts about the area have to be dispelled," said Rosati, adding that attempts by Russia to regain control over the region would be resisted.

"History has shown that conflicts in central Europe cannot be contained and can spread all over the world. This is very dangerous...We cannot have a situation where non-members are being implicitly included in the Russian sphere of influence."
Rosati also said that those countries not invited to become members of NATO in July should be given guarantees that if they achieved the right criteria they would eventually be allowed in.
"There is still a risk that a sequence of wrong decisions might undermine what Europe has achieved in the past and might achieve in future," he said.
Warsaw is trying to maintain stable relations with Moscow ahead of the NATO summit but is angry that Russian authorities have detained a Polish fishing trawler in the Far East.
Rosati said he hoped the two sides could solve the problem in the next few days. "It would be a most stupid thing if an incident in a remote sea could spoil relations between two countries," he said.
Polish Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz said on Tuesday the incident could have been engineered by those in Moscow who wanted relations with Poland to worsen.
